Well, let me think about this season. At my age, with just me and the old lady at home, I can't be too ambitious. 45 years on this land — I know what she gives back.

My 7 mu breaks down like this: I've got about 5 mu in the main plot for wheat-maize double cropping — that's the bread and butter. Then maybe 1.5 mu on a separate piece where I grow cotton every year (the soil's a bit sandier there, cotton does alright). The other 0.5 mu I split between mungbean and red bean — those are mostly for the house, some for the market when prices are good. Beans don't need much, and my wife handles most of that.

For wheat, I'll put down my compound fertilizer before planting in October, then topdress urea at jointing in spring. The extension guy at the township said 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I usually do a bit more — maybe 18 — because I'd rather spend the extra 30 yuan than see yellow leaves. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu, not bad for our land.

For maize after wheat — tight turnaround, usually less than a week. I use a hybrid seed from the agro shop, nothing fancy. Direct seed right after wheat harvest, one base fertilizer, one topdress at big flare stage. Rain usually covers most of it; I pump well water maybe once or twice if July is dry.

Cotton is more work but the price has been okay. I don't use as much fertilizer — cotton doesn't like too much N, it grows leaves instead of bolls. I spray for bollworm maybe 3-4 times through summer.

Beans — I plant them after wheat on that small patch. Hardly any fertilizer, they make their own. Good rotation, keeps the soil healthy.

My main worry this year is the well — pumping costs keep going up. I'll try to irrigate only when I really have to. Labor is my biggest constraint — at 60 with just the two of us, hiring for cotton picking in September is unavoidable, probably 3-4 days.
